comparison: Perfect agreement on optimal memory findings (C44-C47, C141, C235-C238). Both evaluations find the evidence compelling, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming the optimal memory length result and noting convergence with independent computational approaches.

Strong agreement on adaptive memory approach (C48, C145, C149-C151, C239-C240). Both evaluations support the finding that adaptive memory approaches optimal performance without prior information. Peer reviewers highlight this as a 'key innovation' in the methodology.

Strong agreement on methodological framework (C36-C41, C80, C85-C86). Both evaluations affirm the interpretable olfactory state representation. Peer reviewers explicitly praise this as a 'key innovation' and strength of the approach, emphasizing interpretability.

Strong agreement on successful navigation using olfactory-only states (C118-C120, C126, C202). Both evaluations find the approach 'clear and convincing' with 'compelling' evidence. Peer reviewers also reference C211-C212, C220-C221 regarding the two-strategy approach.

Agreement on learned recovery strategies resembling biological behavior (C160-C161, C214-C215). OpenEval focuses on C50-C52, C167-C168, C220 regarding learned recovery performance. Peer reviewers emphasize biological parallels (C179-C181) and accept findings while suggesting future comparative work.

Agreement on generalization across environments (C56-C57, C192-C194, C199-C200). Both evaluations affirm robustness findings. Peer reviewers note 'comprehensive performance analysis' and 'versatility of the approach' across different conditions.

Agreement on spatial-temporal connection and void state localization (C53-C55, C177-C178). OpenEval notes interpretive nature of temporal-spatial inference. Peer reviewers accept spatial findings (C50-C51, C167-C168) as evidence that temporal features predict plume exit.

Agreement on recovery strategy comparisons (C165, C196-C197, C219). Both evaluations accept the comparative analysis and parameter sensitivity findings. Peer reviewers note 'thorough analysis' of recovery strategies and trade-offs.

Divergence on state space optimization (C169-C170, C222-C223). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on Figure 4 and supplement data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning whether minimal representation has been identified and suggesting this remains an open question for future work.

Agreement on limitations of map-free approach (C203-C204, C207-C210). Both evaluations accept the acknowledged limitation of requiring plume proximity. Peer reviewers do not dispute this characterization, noting offsetting advantages in biological realism.

Agreement on core two-strategy algorithmic approach (C211-C213, C221). OpenEval groups these as describing the overall strategy. Peer reviewers reference these claims when discussing the successful navigation results and learned behaviors.

Divergence on methodological choices (C95-C96, C101, C105, C127-C128). OpenEval rates training methodology as straightforwardly SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN (C58, C95-C96), questioning biological relevance of discrete actions and allocentric frame, noting tabular Q-learning is 'both a strength and a limitation.'

Partial overlap on recovery behavior characterization (C171-C174, C179-C181). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative characterization from Figure 4 and Table 1. Peer reviewers reference these claims when discussing biological parallels to animal behaviors.

OpenEval finds spatial distributions at different memory values (C131, C135, C137-C138, C140) well-supported by Figure 2C and supplements. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these mechanistic details of memory-delay relationships.
